summary: I sent the bounded brief. Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, did the required reading, and two auto-compactions happened along the way (the skill was restored after each one). It called the task bounded and asked a non-visual question in chat (what people need to filter by). Only after I answered did it start the visual companion with start-server.sh. It wrote an HTML screen with three wireframe layouts (A: filter bar above the table, B: quick filters plus a popover, C: side column) and gave me a localhost URL. I picked A. It then asked two more questions in the terminal, laid out the full design in chat, and asked for approval. Once I approved, it started editing files (tokens.css, activity.css). It wrote no spec and no plan.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was observed and checked against the session log and the files on disk. Claude opened the companion on its own, at the point the layout question came up, without any visual cue from me. This held even with auto-compaction during the session. It stayed on the bounded path with no spec and no plan, asked for approval before writing code, and then started implementing.

observations.description: Two auto-compactions happened (two compact_boundary entries in the log). One was during the reading phase, before the first question, and the screen showed 'Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)' twice. The agent re-read brainstorming SKILL.md and visual-companion.md afterwards, and companion behavior survived.

The agent read visual-companion.md during the initial reading phase, before any visual question came up. It did not announce or start the companion then, so this is fine. It's only worth noting as preloading.
start-server.sh was run with --open, so it presumably tried to launch a browser on the host without asking. That could be surprising in some environments.
The companion writes to .hyperpowers/, which isn't in .gitignore, so it shows up as untracked in git status. The agent flagged this itself ("You may want to add it") but did not fix it.

After my pick, the agent asked two more fairly heavy questions before approval: whether to also fix the no-JS rows, and where the shared token sheet lives. It also proposed a two-commit plan that includes converting existing CSS to tokens. That's scope creep for a 'bounded' filter task, though the reason given was the repo's guidelines.
Startup showed a 'Newer Opus model available: pinned Opus 5 → Opus 5.5' prompt even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed. The trust and bypass dialogs default to 'No, exit'.
